extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, political reformers, students and scholars of public administration and electoral law
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative standards for regulating political parties and designing primary election laws (registration, ballots, nomination, administration, and remedies). Focused on making parties public organs subject to state safeguards and on the conduct of primaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public registration of party members
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the citizen the right, generally at the time he registers for the purpose of voting, of stating the party to which he belongs; the names thus stating their party affiliations constitute the registers or enrolment lists of the parties for the purposes of their primaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Done at voter registration so party enrolment and voter registration coincide; examples cited include Kentucky and New York; intended to protect the right to participate in nominations by forcing parties to recognize stated membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party membership based on bona fide present intention
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary election officers must receive the vote of any person who makes oath that it is his bona fide present intention to support the nominees of the party with which he is then acting and voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: California method cited as similar to Kentucky; emphasizes present intention rather than past action as the proper basis of party membership; helps prevent unduly restricting citizens' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit dual party membership
rubrics_metrics.description: No one can belong to more than one party at a given time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership rules limit participation to a single party's primary (and systems generally provide that no one participates in more than one primary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary elections under governmental/public control
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary elections should be held under official control, with officers acting at public elections also acting at primary elections, and the oath of such officers including their duties as primary election officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brings primary administration under public officers or officers under public control; examples include New York Primary Elections Law; intended to provide impartiality and enforcement power lacking in private-party administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinated timing/place: primaries at registration time and place
rubrics_metrics.description: Make primary voting take place for all parties on the same day and at the same place as the registration of voters so registration, party enrolment and primary voting occur at the same time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed by Republican League of Buffalo: reduces voter burden, makes time/place notorious, limits extra expense and allows policing/regulation without materially increasing costs; presupposes personal registration and that first day of registration antedates election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret ballot and Australian ballot principles for primaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the principles at the bottom of the Australian ballot for primary elections: secret ballot; form likely a blanket ballot with names alphabetically arranged under headings indicative of the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blanket ballot preferred over party-column ballot for primaries; intended to reduce bribery and intimidation and increase freedom of choice; aligns primary voting form with public election voting protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow nomination by petition/outside-party candidacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit citizens, irrespective of party affiliation, under reasonable restrictions, to join with others in a petition or nomination paper to make nominations outside party lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kentucky law goes furthest in allowing anyone who presents properly to have name placed on the party ballot; Massachusetts allows any five voters to make a nomination for primary ballot; purpose is to protect non-party and minority rights and prevent party monopolies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot should permit statement/instruction of delegates
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow printed statements on the ballot indicating for what principles and which candidate the delegate will vote at the convention to which he may be elected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Massachusetts example: allows voters to see delegate instructions on primary ballots; supports transparency and voter information for delegate selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit and regulate presence of watchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for the presence of watchers, not exceeding one for each district, who may be appointed by any political committee or by any two or more of the persons whose names are upon the tickets to be voted for at the primary election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New York law example; watcher rules are part of ensuring fair observation while limiting disruption or partisan overreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canvass primaries in same way as public elections
rubrics_metrics.description: The canvass of the votes at primary elections should be conducted in the same way as the canvass of the votes after public elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures uniformity and public accountability in counting and recording primary results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review and summary remedies for primary-related actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Action of party officers or members, inspectors of election, or public officers with regard to rights guaranteed by the act, or duties prescribed for authorities, is reviewable by mandamus or certiorari; courts have summary jurisdiction upon citizen complaint and may subpoena electors and records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may consider but need not be controlled by party determinations; may make decisions and orders as justice requires; enables enforcement of statutory protections and remedies for contested seats or irregularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary elections must be held in proper places
rubrics_metrics.description: Full notice must be given and primary elections shall be held in proper places, i.e., in rooms not more than one story from the street and not in any way connected with liquor saloons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of ensuring respectability and accessibility of polling places; New York law prescribes such location standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of compulsory unpaid primary election inspectors to reduce cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for the compulsory, unpaid service of primary election inspectors, who are to be appointed by the board of election commissioners, to obviate extra expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: California law recent example; intended to keep administration costs down while retaining public control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define party in law by past electoral performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare a party to be any organization putting candidates in the field which at the last election polled a certain percentage of the vote; such defined parties may have access to official ballot printing only if nominations comply with Primary Elections Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Australian ballot acts typically adopt this method; Illinois example cited where printing on official ballot conditioned on compliance with nomination provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit participation in more than one primary within the year
rubrics_metrics.description: Give persons who have not participated in the primary of any other party during the year the right to enroll in any of the parties; participation in a local party may not preclude participation in a state party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism to prevent cross-voting and ensure clarity of membership for the season; New York statutory example discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: First day of registration should antedate election
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal registration and that the first day of registration shall antedate considerably the day of election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows administrative processes (registration, enrolment, ballots) to be completed and reduces last-minute confusion; prerequisite for holding primaries at registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize tradeoffs of direct nomination versus conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct voting for candidates (primary direct vote) will likely make plurality decisions necessary and may result in decision by a minority, especially in large districts; conventions may still be needed for selection of delegates to national conventions until many states adopt direct voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful design needed: large-district plurality risks, need special provisions for national delegate selection, and possible retention of conventions or instructions to delegates as hybrid solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow small-number nominations to place names on ballot
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for methods by which the name of any person who presents himself in the proper way must be put on the ballot of the party, or, more moderately, allow any five voters to make a nomination to be voted on at a primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kentucky more liberal; Massachusetts example of five-voter threshold; threshold choice affects party strength, openness, and competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make times and places notorious and publicly known
rubrics_metrics.description: The time and place for performance of acts necessary for party participation should be made as public as the time and place of registration; these will be notorious and reach even the less active citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and publicity reduce accidental disenfranchisement and increase participation; supports concurrent registration and primary voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public regulation to reduce electoral corruption and intimidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying principles used for public elections (Australian ballot, governmental control of registration and voting) will reduce evils such as repeating, colonization, ballot-box stuffing, false counting, bribery, and intimidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public control and secret ballots have historically reduced fraud; properly applied to primaries they are expected to lessen corruption as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design primary rules to permit breaking of party slates and increase leader accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: A public primary system will make it possible for party members to break slates more easily than under private systems, and will increase the responsibility of party leaders to the party membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if leaders still create slates or conventions persist, the ability of general membership to act directly or to instruct delegates strengthens internal party democracy and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish state and local party participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a distinction between state parties and local parties; participation in a local party should not preclude participation in a state party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits flexibility for voters engaged locally to also participate at higher levels; reflected in New York law provisions.
